comparator.name: Biologie (Biology)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current student curriculum fixes a three-year, 180-EC bachelor comprising a 135-EC Biology major and 45 EC of profiling space. The first year contains eight 7.5-EC courses: seven named compulsory foundations and one restricted first-year choice. After year one, only Academic Communication (level 2) and the 15-EC Afstudeerproject (level 3) remain compulsory; the remainder of the major is selected from Biology courses. The current study guide confirms that ordinary courses are 7.5 EC unless stated otherwise and that the Afstudeerproject is the 15-EC exception. The graduation-project page confirms that the compulsory project combines practical biological research, a report and presentation. The prospective curriculum presents eleven study-interest directions as advice for building a coherent programme, not formal tracks, so no direction is selected or named as the comparator route. The 52.5 EC of later Biology choice and 45 EC profiling space remain genuine choice space. These components account for exactly 180 EC without inventing electives.
components: Official restricted choice retained without inventing a course.
Seven 7.5-EC Biology courses selected coherently from the current level-2 and level-3 offer; retained as genuine choice space.
Compulsory level-3 practical research project, report and presentation.
Genuine profiling space for electives, a minor, education minor or other approved study.

alternatives.label: Biological sciences: cells, organisms and ecosystems
alternatives.labelReason: The programme spans biological organisation from molecules and cells through physiology, organisms, biodiversity and ecosystems, supported by laboratory, statistical and data methods.
alternatives.concept: A broad biology programme moving from cellular and biochemical mechanisms to physiology, organisms, evolution, biodiversity and ecosystems, with laboratory work, statistics, programming and data analysis.
progression: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes every HCB course that formally requires it. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics. Programming, mathematics and introductory biological courses precede advanced data, molecular, biomedical and environmental work. Every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Molecular, cellular and biomedical biology
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular-cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, immunology, physiology and experimental/data methods form a coherent health-facing biological direction supported by the programme’s cells, genomics, bioinformatics, neurobiology and health interests.
alternatives.concept: Focuses on cellular function, biomolecules, genetics, host–microbe interaction, physiology and disease, then adds neurobiology and computational methods for analysing complex biological and biomedical systems.
progression: The life-science and brain gateways precede every course that formally requires them; Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics and Neural Networks & Deep Learning. Molecular-cell, laboratory and neurobiology foundations precede advanced genetics, disease, immunology, pharmacology, cognition and computational work. Every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad biological-sciences route, this programme replaces introductory biodiversity, conservation biology, ecosystems, evolution, soils, marine biology and sustainability governance with a brain-and-behaviour gateway, neural networks, perception, higher-order functions, machine learning, psycholinguistics and image processing. Seven courses differ in each direction, producing a substantially more molecular, biomedical and computational programme.

alternatives.label: Ecology, evolution and conservation biology
alternatives.labelReason: Evolution, biodiversity, ecosystems, conservation, climate, biogeochemistry and field-oriented environmental research form a coherent direction grounded in explicit programme interests and current Biology study-interest guidance.
alternatives.concept: Centres evolution, biodiversity, ecological processes and conservation while retaining cellular, physiological, microbial, laboratory and statistical foundations. Climate, soils, biogeochemistry, marine biology and delta research connect organisms and ecosystems to environmental change and management.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II and Environmental Biogeochemistry. Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes Molecular Cell Biology, Life Science Laboratory and Infection & Immunity; Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics. Introductory biodiversity, evolution and sustainability work precedes advanced conservation, ecology, marine biology, biogeochemistry and delta research. Every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: This route shifts decisively from the molecular/biomedical alternative to populations, ecosystems and environmental change. It replaces the brain-and-behaviour gateway, biochemistry, anatomy, genetics/pathology, disease, pharmacology and six cognition/data courses with biodiversity, evolution, conservation, ecosystems, sustainability foundations, climate, Earth systems, sustainable farming, soils, marine biology, biogeochemistry, delta research and sustainability governance.

core: Living organisms and biological systems from molecules to ecosystems
Genes, genomes, cells, biomolecules and molecular mechanisms
Plants, animals, microorganisms, physiology and organismal biology
Biological modelling, statistics, genomics, bioinformatics and quantitative evidence
Experimental, laboratory, field and independent biological research
adjacent: Health, biomedical research, biotechnology and toxicology
Human impacts, environmental change and nature conservation
Neurobiology and biological bases of behaviour
questions: How do biological systems function from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems?
How do evolution and human activity shape biodiversity, ecosystems and conservation needs?
How can molecular, computational and experimental biology address health challenges?

candidates.label: Educational minor in biology teaching
candidates.reason: The educational minor is a supported selectable direction, but the three-alternative limit is reached. It is also a teacher-preparation option layered onto Biology rather than a stronger substitute for the three included disciplinary Biology pathways.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers the programme's full molecules-to-ecosystems identity. Two direct programme-interest clusters then support coherent, substantially distinct alternatives: molecular/cellular biology applied to health and computation, and ecology/evolution/conservation applied to environmental change. All three use feasible 24-course schedules and differ by well over four courses where required. Production stops at the maximum of three defensible alternatives.

notes.text: Utrecht Biology combines seven compulsory first-year foundations, flexible advanced Biology choices and a compulsory 15-EC research graduation project. UCR can assemble broad, molecular/biomedical and ecology/evolution programmes from current courses, but it does not reproduce Utrecht's dedicated organismal and plant sequence, its full specialist elective catalogue or its required graduation project; shared rows show substantive overlap rather than full equivalence.
